*** SPRINT 75 / V0.29.30: 3 of 11 closed, 2 PASSING (US-561, US-563), 1 blocked-by-hardware (US-560/BL-034). NEXT ITERATION PICKS UP US-566 (powerwatch arm logging, size S) per the fixed closeout order -- nothing blocks it. ***

*** US-563 CLOSED passes:true -- drive_summary must not read as assessed before it is assessed. Three schema truths (v0024) + the durable applied-schema guard. Full AC-by-AC detail in sprint.json completionNotes; reusable lessons below. ***

THE LESSON THAT PAID OFF, AGAIN, AND IT IS NOW 3 SPRINTS RUNNING: I RE-MEASURED THE PREMISE INSTEAD OF INHERITING IT, AND THE MEASUREMENT WIDENED THE STORY. A read-only information_schema probe against live prod (`bash offices/pm/scripts/prod_db_query.sh "<SELECT>"` -- WORKS FROM THIS HARNESS, no creds needed, ~5s) returned drives.data_quality DEFAULT 'full', drive_statistics.data_quality DEFAULT 'full', drive_summary.data_quality DEFAULT 'full', is_real DEFAULT 0, ambient_temp_at_start_c still present. **AC-2 names ONLY drive_summary -- but the verdict-shaped default was on ALL THREE tables.** Building to the story text would have fixed the one column that had already embarrassed us and left two loaded identically. GENERALISE: when a story hands you a schema fact, the probe that confirms it costs seconds and is the same probe that tells you the story's SCOPE was too narrow. US-560 taught this (fabricated fixture), US-561 applied it (journalctl RC), US-563 got a scope correction out of it.

THE CARVE-OUT I REFUSED, AND WHY IT IS THE WHOLE POINT: the tempting exemption was 'drives and drive_statistics are always written with an explicit data_quality, so leave their defaults alone'. Refused. **'The writer always sets it' is a claim about INTENT, never about ENFORCEMENT** -- that is precisely specs/anti-patterns.md's inert guard, and it is the same reasoning that let the drive_summary default sit unnoticed until it misled two agents. The applied-schema guard makes no carve-outs either.

THE DURABLE HALF IS THE GUARD, NOT THE TWO DEFAULTS. Atlas insisted it carry its OWN acceptance line and OWN test because folded in as prose it gets built as 'change two defaults' and quietly does not happen. He was right, and the way to make it durable was (a) assert COLUMN DEFAULTS not just presence/type, (b) make it DISCOVERY-DRIVEN -- ask information_schema which tables carry the column rather than hard-coding a list, so a table added tomorrow is covered with zero edits, and (c) give it a NEGATIVE SELF-TEST. **A guard that has never been SEEN to fail is not known to be a guard** -- so it is parametrised over every assessed verdict, over a table that does not exist yet, and over is_real=0 AND is_real=1.

NAMING WAS THE ROOT CAUSE, NOT THE DEFAULT VALUE. One constant (DRIVE_SUMMARY_DATA_QUALITY_DEFAULT) did double duty as BOTH 'the column default' AND 'the clean verdict'. **That conflation made the defect UNSAYABLE IN CODE: there was no name for 'not yet assessed' because the default WAS a verdict.** Split into *_FULL / *_ASSESSED_*_VALUES / *_VALUES / *_COLUMN_DEFAULT, each named for its layer. When a defect feels like it 'should have been obvious', check whether the vocabulary allowed anyone to state it.

ORDERING INSIDE A MIGRATION CAN BE SILENTLY LOAD-BEARING: widen every CHECK to admit 'unassessed' BEFORE moving any DEFAULT. Setting a default the CHECK forbids does NOT fail at ALTER time -- **it fails on the next INSERT that omits the column, i.e. on the next Pi sync, in the car.** Pinned by test. Each substep idempotent + post-condition probe, so a half-applied run is re-runnable.

DO NOT REWRITE EXISTING ROWS. A DEFAULT applies to future INSERTs only, and the migration CANNOT distinguish a genuine batch 'full' from a pre-computed default without re-running analytics. Back-filling 'probably unassessed' would MANUFACTURE a reading -- the corollary to 'land what you read'. Left alone; the nightly batch overwrites each row when it assesses it.

*** VERIFY 'MY CHANGE BROKE THIS' BEFORE BELIEVING IT -- I ALMOST INHERITED THREE FAILURES THAT WERE NOT MINE. tests/server exits 1 with exactly 3 FAILED. Two are stale tail pins (versions[-1]=='0015'/'0019'); `git show HEAD:src/server/migrations/__init__.py` proved the tail was ALREADY '0023', so appending v0024 changed the reported VALUE, not the failure -- already TD-062. The third (test_sync::test_allAcceptedTables, 'pi_state' extra) deserved REAL suspicion because US-563 modified sync.py -- but my diff adds no table, and `git show HEAD:src/server/api/sync.py` already had "pi_state" at line 214 from US-453. Pre-existing, uncovered, so I filed TD-082. **`git show HEAD:<file>` is the cheap, non-destructive way to answer 'was this red before me' WITHOUT stash** (stash is not on Ralph's allow-list and would risk the uncommitted tree). *** 

FLAGGED NOT SWALLOWED: TD-083 -- the PI's local drive_summary STILL spells the column ambient_temp_at_start_c. The server renamed; sync.py maps the legacy key so the Pi's value still LANDS (no flag day, no deploy coupling), but the same mislabel lives on the other tier. Renameable in any later sprint precisely because that seam exists.

OWED AT DEPLOY, NOT CLAIMED: validationCriteria #1 (applied prod schema AFTER migration) and #3 (read a pending drive) need v0024 to actually RUN, and applying a migration to prod is a DEPLOY action PM owns. I measured the BEFORE state only. The guard IS that check: 2 live tests skip with a PRINTED reason and run against chi-srv-01 when OBD2_APPLIED_SCHEMA_TEST=1. **PM: run them after deploying V0.29.30 and #1 + #3 close together.**

ENVIRONMENT (all re-confirmed this session): **`offices/pm/scripts/prod_db_query.sh` WORKS from this harness for read-only prod SQL -- new and useful.** Pi reachable via `ssh -o BatchMode=yes chi-eclipse-01`. `make` NOT on PATH (exits 127, **which reads like a pass**) -- use `python -m ruff check <files>`; mypy NOT installed. **The Bash tool refuses compound commands (`a; b`, `a && b`)** -- one per call. **`grep -rn` over the repo TIMES OUT at 120s on this SMB share -- use the Grep tool (ripgrep), it returns instantly.** `pytest -q` prints no summary on this tree: redirect, then `echo $?` AND `grep -cE '^(FAILED|ERROR)'`; a plain (non-`-q`) run DOES print 'N passed'. **`@'...'@` PowerShell here-strings LEAK LITERAL @ LINES into a Bash `git commit -m`** -- I had to amend the subject; use a `<<'EOF'` heredoc with `git commit -F -`. Scratch files must live in the repo (/tmp not writable) and be rm'd before committing. Index lock CLEAR all session.
